page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16-lssd is an x86_64 instance provisioned with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 504 MB L3 cache, alongside vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8). The hardware configuration includes 124.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, and integrates 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across two local drives. No dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core and compression performance. In Geekbench, the instance scored 2256.0 in single-core testing and achieved top-tier throughput in text processing (2913.0). Single-threaded data compression is equally capable, reaching 36.02 GB/sec in gzip compression and 15.11 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, placing in the top quartile. Small-model LLM text generation (135M model) also demonstrated top-tier output at 366.16 tokens per second, benefiting from Intel AMX instruction support. Multi-core compute and broader system tests, including stress-ng multi-core (17938.08), PassMark CPU (30658.13), and memory bandwidth (133.46 GB/sec large-block read), perform within average thresholds relative to peer hardware.

The combination of high memory density, substantial L3 cache, and bundled low-latency NVMe scratch disks yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for input/output-intensive and in-memory operations. Tradeoffs include standard multi-threaded throughput that scales strictly with its 8 physical cores, along with the lack of permanent persistence inherent to ephemeral local SSD configurations. The instance is suited for high-throughput in-memory caching such as Redis, analytical databases, local build and CI/CD pipelines, compression-heavy ETL flows, and moderate scale AI inference workloads.
